title: Basic Safeguarding of Covered Contractor Information Systems
summary: Requires 15 basic security controls for protecting Federal Contract Information (FCI) on contractor information systems.

title: Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting
summary: Requires implementation of NIST SP 800-171 security requirements and reporting of cyber incidents affecting covered defense information within 72 hours.

title: Notice of NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment Requirements
summary: Requires an offeror to have a current NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment posted in SPRS prior to award.

title: NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment Requirements
summary: Requires contractors to provide the Government access to conduct or verify NIST SP 800-171 assessments and flow down the requirement to subcontractors.

title: Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Requirements
summary: Requires the contractor to have a current CMMC certificate at the level specified in the contract before award.

title: Cloud Computing Services
summary: Establishes requirements for cloud service providers, including FedRAMP moderate baseline authorization and incident reporting.

title: Compliance with Safeguarding Covered Defense Information Controls
summary: Requires offerors to represent compliance with NIST SP 800-171 or identify any not yet implemented requirements via a system security plan and plans of action.

title: Prohibition on Contracting for Certain Telecommunications and Video Surveillance Services or Equipment
summary: Prohibits contractors from providing or using covered telecommunications equipment or services as a substantial or essential component of any system.

title: Contractor Purchasing System Administration
summary: Establishes requirements for an approved contractor purchasing system for managing subcontracts and purchases.

title: Export-Controlled Items
summary: Requires the contractor to comply with all applicable export control laws and regulations.

title: Sources of Electronic Parts
summary: Requires contractors to obtain electronic parts from trusted sources to prevent counterfeit parts from entering the supply chain.

title: Contractor Code of Business Ethics and Conduct
summary: Requires contractors to have a written code of business ethics and an internal control system, and to display fraud hotline posters.

title: Item Unique Identification and Valuation
summary: Requires unique item identification (UID) marking on qualifying deliverable items.

title: Limitations on Subcontracting
summary: Limits the percentage of contract cost a small business concern may subcontract to non-similarly-situated entities.

title: Prohibition of Hexavalent Chromium
summary: Restricts the use of hexavalent chromium in specified coatings and materials on deliverable items.

title: Rights in Technical Data—Other Than Commercial Products and Commercial Services
summary: Establishes the Government's license rights in technical data (other than computer software documentation) for items, components, or processes that are not commercial products/services or were developed in whole or part at Government expense. Grants unlimited rights, government purpose rights (a default 5-year period), limited rights, or specifically negotiated rights depending on how development was funded. All rights not expressly granted to the Government are retained by the Contractor, and data delivered without a proper restrictive marking is presumed furnished with unlimited rights.

title: Unlimited Rights in Technical Data (252.227-7013(c)(1))
summary: The Government has unlimited rights (use, modify, reproduce, perform, display, release, or disclose in any manner, for any purpose) in technical data developed exclusively with Government funds, form/fit/function data, data necessary for installation/operation/maintenance/training (other than detailed manufacturing or process data), studies/analyses/test data required as a contract deliverable, and data that is otherwise publicly available or was previously released without restriction.

title: Government Purpose Rights in Technical Data (252.227-7013(c)(2))
summary: For technical data pertaining to items or processes developed with mixed (partly Government, partly private) funding, the Government receives government purpose rights: unrestricted use within the Government, plus the right to release outside the Government to authorized recipients for U.S. Government purposes only (not commercial use). This default lasts 5 years from contract/modification execution (or a negotiated period), after which the data converts to unlimited rights; during that period the Contractor retains the exclusive right to commercial use, including licensing others.

title: Limited Rights and Marking Requirements (252.227-7013(c)(3), (g))
summary: Technical data pertaining to items or processes developed exclusively at private expense carries only limited rights: usable within the Government, but not releasable outside the Government, not usable for manufacture, and not authorized for use by others without the Contractor's written permission — with narrow exceptions for emergency repair/overhaul and release to covered Government support contractors under nondisclosure. Contractors must conspicuously mark each page/item with the appropriate legend (limited rights, government purpose rights, or special license rights) to assert restrictions; data delivered without such a marking is presumed furnished with unlimited rights.

title: Rights in Other Than Commercial Computer Software and Other Than Commercial Computer Software Documentation
summary: Establishes the Government's license rights in computer software and computer software documentation that do not qualify as commercial computer software: unlimited rights, government purpose rights (a default 5-year period), restricted rights, or specifically negotiated rights, depending on funding source. Unlike 252.227-7013's 'limited rights' for technical data, privately-funded software instead carries 'restricted rights' — a narrower, software-specific set of permitted uses. All rights not granted to the Government are retained by the Contractor, and unmarked deliverables are presumed furnished with unlimited rights.

title: Unlimited Rights in Computer Software (252.227-7014(c)(1))
summary: The Government has unlimited rights in computer software developed exclusively with Government funds, in all computer software documentation required to be delivered under the contract (regardless of how the underlying software was funded), and in software/documentation that is otherwise publicly available or was previously released without restriction.

title: Government Purpose Rights in Computer Software (252.227-7014(c)(2))
summary: Computer software developed with mixed funding carries government purpose rights for a default 5-year period — full Government use plus release to authorized recipients for U.S. Government purposes, but not commercial use — after which it converts to unlimited rights, mirroring the treatment of mixed-funded technical data under 252.227-7013.

title: Restricted Rights and Marking Requirements (252.227-7014(c)(3), (g))
summary: Other than commercial computer software developed exclusively at private expense carries only restricted rights: use on one computer at a time, a reasonable number of copies for backup/archive/modification, and narrow rights to modify or permit contractors to diagnose/correct/adapt the software under nondisclosure — with no right to decompile, disassemble, or reverse-engineer beyond what's authorized. As with 252.227-7013, the Contractor must mark each item with the appropriate restrictive legend or the software is presumed delivered with unlimited rights.
